## Register and classify block faces (`boundary-condition/external/*`) {#sec-ch11-registry}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0
status: draft
-->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Face callbacks fill physical ghosts; layout exchange supplies internal and wrapped faces. Classification depends on the predicate used, not only on the boundary label.
Default: reflecting.
Order: exact discrete operation or local derivation below; coupled solver order not measured.
:::

### Derivation

This is dispatch infrastructure, so there is no differential equation to discretize. A face is physical exactly
when its callback exists. A diffusion wall is a physical face with a recorded reflecting or fixed-temperature name.
The hydro predicate `is_x1_wall` instead accepts physical x1 faces whose names do not start with `periodic`.
These are different sets: an outflow face passes the hydro predicate but not the diffusion whitelist.
This follows directly from `is_wall_boundary` ([`meshblock_options.cpp:218-271`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp#L218-L271)) and `is_x1_wall` ([`hydro.cpp:204-209`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L204-L209)).

A repeated fill must reproduce the same ghost values from the owned slab. This is an idempotence contract,
not a guarantee for arbitrary callbacks: the registry comment requires it because a callback also runs on a
thin tangential ghost slab (`BC_FUNCTION`, [`bc_func.hpp:14-39`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.hpp#L14-L39)). Check C1 exercises this contract for the built-in mirror
and copy rules; no spatial order is assigned to dispatch.

The report-only checks are `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`; their current output is
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`. They do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The face order is x1 inner/outer, x2 inner/outer, x3 inner/outer. In a four-dimensional hydro tensor these
map to dimensions 3, 2 and 1. Context carries EOS, coordinates, references, representation and ghost width.
Construction nulls exchange-owned callbacks for slab/cubed layouts; the cubed-sphere branch is separate.
A non-null custom callback therefore still counts as physical. No accuracy order follows from classification.

: Implementation sites for registry. {#tbl-ch11-registry-code}

1. Validate YAML keys and append `_inner` or `_outer`; reject names absent from the registry. The anchor `periodic_z` is in [`meshblock_options.cpp:88-127`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp#L88-L127).
2. Set layout periodic flags, then null callbacks owned by exchange during construction. The anchor `bfuncs` is in [`meshblock.cpp:138-166`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L138-L166).
3. Classify at the consuming operator: unnamed programmatic callbacks warn once and return false for the diffusion wall test. The anchor `is_wall_boundary` is in [`meshblock_options.cpp:218-271`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp#L218-L271).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The fixed-temperature names occur in the whitelist, but no built-in registration is present in the boundary
implementation inspected here. They do not establish an available thermal BC. The comment calling outflow
zero-gradient in `is_wall_boundary` is stale relative to the characteristic implementation ([`meshblock_options.cpp:218-271`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp#L218-L271),
[`bc_func.cpp:108-133`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L108-L133)). Cubed-sphere custom panel faces require care wherever a physical-face test is used.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result is claimed.
:::
